sources.entry: HortusFox - Collaborative plant management and tracking system for plant enthusiasts. (Source Code) MIT PHP/Docker

summary.one_liner: HortusFox is a free, self-hosted, collaborative plant management and tracking system built in PHP, with per-location plant organization, tasks, inventory, calendar, and group chat.
summary.what_it_does: HortusFox lets users track plants assigned to locations, with attributes, photos, notes, and logs for each plant. It includes a task system with reminders, an inventory system, a calendar with classes, a search feature, and a history feature. A collaborative group chat, a weather forecast feature (via OpenWeatherMap), and QR codes are included. Plant identification uses the Pl@ntNet API, and plant data queries use the Global Biodiversity Information Facility. The app offers a theme system, an admin dashboard, automatic and manual backups, a REST API, and console commands for migrations, themes, and backup import/export. Cronjob endpoints handle overdue and recurring task notices, calendar reminders, and automatic backups.
use_cases: track care and watering schedules for houseplants
manage plants by room or garden location
share plant records with household members
keep an inventory of plant supplies and fertilizers
self-host a plant journal with backups
how_to_run: git clone the repository and cd hortusfox-web
Edit environment variables (admin login, timezone, database settings) in docker-compose.yml
Open the application in a browser and log in with the admin credentials set in docker-compose.yml
notable: Per-location design: every plant is assigned to a location
Integrated REST API for third-party software
Theme system for customizing the workspace look
Installer, Docker, and manual installation paths
Cronjob endpoints and console commands for maintenance and backups
caveats: Weather forecast and plant identification require the user to obtain their own OpenWeatherMap and Pl@ntNet API keys
System requirements include PHP ^8.3 and MariaDB ^11.4 plus an SMTP server for email
Application testing is marked as under construction in the README
